What is Playwright?

How do I launch a browser using Playwright Python?

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
browser = p.chromium.launch()
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto("https://example.com")
print(page.title())
browser.close()
This example launches Chromium, creates a page, navigates to a URL, prints the page title, and closes the browser.

Explain what machine learning is.

Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence in which a model learns patterns from data. Instead of explicitly programming every rule, the system uses examples to learn relationships and make predictions or decisions. Common types of machine learning include supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.

What is artificial intelligence?

Explain deep learning in simple terms.

Deep learning is a type of machine learning that uses neural networks with multiple computational layers. Each layer transforms information into increasingly useful representations. Deep learning is commonly used for image recognition, speech processing, language modeling, and other complex tasks.

What is a neural network?

A neural network is a computational model made of interconnected units called neurons. The network receives input values, transforms them using learned weights, biases, and activation functions, and produces an output. During training, the model adjusts its parameters to reduce prediction errors.

What is a transformer model?

A transformer is a neural network architecture designed to process sequences using attention mechanisms. Attention allows the model to consider relationships between different tokens in a sequence. Transformers are widely used in language models because they can efficiently model long-range relationships between tokens.

Explain overfitting.

Overfitting occurs when a machine learning model learns the training data too closely and performs poorly on unseen data. A common sign is very low training loss combined with high validation loss. More diverse training data, regularization, dropout, data augmentation, or a smaller model can help reduce overfitting.

What is a validation set?

A validation set is a portion of data that is not used directly to update model parameters during training. It is used to evaluate how well the model generalizes to unseen examples and to help select training settings such as learning rate, model size, and number of epochs.

What is a tokenizer?

A tokenizer converts text into tokens that a language model can process. Tokens may represent words, subwords, characters, or other pieces of text. The tokenizer maps tokens to numerical token IDs, which are then provided to the neural network.

What is a vocabulary?

A vocabulary is the collection of tokens known by a tokenizer. Each token normally has a unique integer ID. Special tokens such as unknown, beginning-of-sequence, and end-of-sequence tokens may also be included.

What is a language model?

A language model learns statistical patterns in sequences of tokens and estimates the probability of the next token given the previous tokens. During training, the model learns to predict target tokens from input sequences. During generation, predicted tokens are repeatedly added to the context.

What is causal language modeling?

Causal language modeling trains a model to predict the next token using only tokens that appear before it. For example, if the input sequence contains "Machine learning is", the model learns to predict the next appropriate token. The target sequence is shifted one position relative to the input sequence.

Why do we need training data?

Training data provides examples from which a machine learning model can learn patterns. The quality, diversity, correctness, and size of the training data strongly influence the resulting model. Poor or repetitive data can cause weak generalization and overfitting.

How can I improve a small language model?

A small language model can be improved by increasing the amount and diversity of training data, improving data quality, tuning the learning rate, reducing overfitting, selecting an appropriate model size, using a suitable tokenizer, and evaluating the model on examples that were not included in training.

What should I do if training loss decreases but validation loss increases?

This usually indicates overfitting. The model is becoming better at memorizing the training data while becoming worse at generalizing to unseen data. Possible solutions include adding more training data, reducing model capacity, increasing regularization, using dropout, stopping training earlier, or improving the validation dataset.

Explain gradient descent.

Gradient descent is an optimization method used to update model parameters so that the training loss decreases. The gradients indicate how the loss changes with respect to each parameter. The optimizer uses these gradients and a learning rate to determine parameter updates.

What is an epoch?

An epoch is one complete pass through the training dataset. If a dataset contains many batches, an epoch consists of processing all those batches once. Training for multiple epochs allows the model to repeatedly learn from the available examples, although too many epochs can cause overfitting.

What is a batch?

A batch is a group of training examples processed together in one optimization step. Batch size controls how many examples are processed before model parameters are updated. Smaller batches generally require less memory but can produce noisier gradient estimates.

What is a checkpoint?

A checkpoint is a saved copy of a model's learned parameters and often its optimizer state and training metadata. Checkpoints allow training to be resumed and make it possible to evaluate or compare models from different training stages.
